questions.question: Which description fits the **DocumentReference** resource?
options: A reference to a document of any kind for any purpose.

A set of healthcare-related information that is assembled together into a single logical package that provides a single coherent statement of meaning, establishes its own context and that has clinical attestation with regard…
A collection of documents compiled for a purpose together with metadata that applies to the collection.
Catalog entries are wrappers that contextualize items included in a catalog.
questions.explanation: **DocumentReference**: A reference to a document of any kind for any purpose. Provides metadata about the document so that the document can be discovered and managed. The scope of a document is any seralized object with a mime-type, so includes formal patient centric documents (CDA), cliical notes, scanned paper, and non-patient specific documents like policy text. The other descriptions belong to **Composition**, **DocumentManifest**, **CatalogEntry**.

questions.question: Which resource would you use? A scanned discharge letter (PDF), stored with its type, date and author so it can be found.
questions.explanation: **DocumentReference**. Metadata about any document, pointing to the content.

questions.question: You know **DocumentReference**. Which resource should you use instead when you need “a structured report of results”?
questions.explanation: **DiagnosticReport**: a structured report of results. **DocumentReference** is for something else: A reference to a document of any kind for any purpose.

questions.question: Which element is **required** (minimum cardinality 1) in every **DocumentReference** instance?
questions.explanation: The required top-level elements of DocumentReference are `status` (1..1), `content` (1..*). The other options have a minimum cardinality of 0, so they are optional.

questions.question: Which element of **DocumentReference** is a **modifier** (?!), so receiving systems must not ignore it?
questions.explanation: Modifier elements of DocumentReference: `status`. `status`: current | superseded | entered-in-error. A modifier can change the meaning of the whole resource: for example, a status of `entered-in-error` means the data must not be used.
